candidates.expected_difficulty: Medium. Central bank and customs sources already on file internally; South Africa retains exchange control regulations administered by SARB (Financial Surveillance Department) that require careful, current-text sourcing.
known_risk_areas: Exchange control relaxation has been gradual and multi-year — cite current effective rules, not historical summaries

P8C-1 source-intake finding (2026-07-23): the on-file cash_declaration_threshold conflates the SARB R25,000 rand exchange-control allowance with the R100,000 excess-currency rule and the SARS customs declaration. Correct in the publication-candidate review: R25,000 = SARB limit on carrying rand; excess currency over R100,000 (or foreign currency convertible to Rand over R100,000) requires SARB written permission; SARS administers the traveller declaration (mandatory online from 1 July 2026, or manual TD-01). Keep exchange control (SARB), customs declaration (SARS), and AML (FIC) distinct.
SARS mandatory online traveller declaration takes effect 1 July 2026 — verify current effective process at the publication-candidate review.

P8C-2 resolution (2026-07-23): content corrected and verified against official SARS pages. R25,000 = SARB rand-carrying limit on SA bank notes (unlimited within the Common Monetary Area; above R25,000 needs prior SARB authorisation) per the SARS Departure page; R100,000 = SARB excess-currency threshold (rand or foreign currency convertible to rand) needing SARB written permission per the SARS Travellers page; the traveller declaration (online form / manual TD-01) is administered by SARS. SARB exchange control, SARS customs declaration and FIC AML kept distinct. Specific resident/non-resident allowance amounts in the Currency and Exchanges Manual PDF remain marked [HARDENING] (no PDF page-pinpoint tooling).

P8C-2a (2026-07-23): consistency correction. P8C-2 wrongly advanced South Africa to publish_ready while resident_holding_rules and non_resident_rules retained [HARDENING], conflicting with the US precedent where unresolved [HARDENING] blocks publish_ready. banking_conversion_practicality was re-examined and also marked [HARDENING] (the FinSurv page confirms the ADLA framework and FICA exist, but the specific licensing/documentary/operational provisions live in the Manual PDFs, not page-pinpointable here). South Africa restored to source_review_ready. Governance rule adopted: any unresolved [HARDENING] on a public rule field blocks publish_ready unless a formal governance exception is explicitly adopted. publish_ready remains BLOCKED until every [HARDENING] marker is cleared with claim-specific pinpointed evidence (e.g. the Currency and Exchanges Manual page references).

P8C-2b (2026-07-23): all three [HARDENING] markers CLEARED with pinpointed evidence from the Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers, live version 2026-06-25 (P8D-0). resident_holding_rules = R2m single discretionary allowance (pp.102,111) + R10m foreign capital allowance (pp.48,111) via Authorised Dealers under SARS TCS; non_resident_rules = non-resident exchange controls abolished / income freely transferable / Non-resident Rand & vostro accounts / retransfer of introduced funds (pp.118,120,197); banking_conversion_practicality = FIC Act s.21 CDD (p.113) + SARB Reporting System purpose codes (p.99). Traveller R25,000 (SARS Departure) and R100,000 (SARS Travellers) remain SARS-sourced and are NOT re-sourced to the Manual; the Manual R25,000 ADLA remittance cap is kept distinct. South Africa advanced source_review_ready -> publish_ready under the P8C-2a consistency rule (no unresolved [HARDENING]).
